title: Wind Vector Retrieval from CFOSAT SWIM Near-Nadir Rotating-Beam Measurements
content: The Surface Waves Investigation and Monitoring instrument (SWIM) on the China–France Oceanography Satellite (CFOSAT) is a Ku-band rotating radar with nadir and five off-nadir beams (2–10°). This study retrieves the wind vector from SWIM's normalized radar cross section (σ⁰) alone and assesses its own direction information. Recalibrated to the Global Precipitation Measurement Ku-band radar, σ⁰ is inverted with a model of stress-equivalent wind and wave height, ERA5 setting the mean level and ambiguity-removal background. Against the Advanced Scatterometer (ASCAT), over 12 million held-out matches of the July 2020–December 2024 record (25 km grid) give, at all winds, a speed bias of 0.07 m s⁻¹ (ASCAT − SWIM) and a standard deviation of 1.37 m s⁻¹; triple collocation of matches within 30 min gives SWIM about twice the ASCAT error. Bias and standard deviation are 0.03 and 0.90 m s⁻¹ against the Haiyang-2 (HY-2) scatterometers at 4–20 m s⁻¹, and 0.00 and 1.36 m s⁻¹ against buoys at all winds. In 2 m s⁻¹ bins of mean wind from 4 to 22 m s⁻¹, the ASCAT bias stays within 0.26 m s⁻¹. With the wave-height term, the buoy wave-height slope is similar to those of ERA5 and HY-2; a residual slope remains against ASCAT. Above 4 m s⁻¹, without weather-model input, the rank-1 direction lies within 45° of ASCAT in 59% of cells.
